parameters.content:
## Publish one daily Pinterest pin with Google Sheets, OpenAI and PinBridge

> Uses the **PinBridge** community node (`n8n-nodes-pinbridge`), verified by n8n, so it installs on n8n Cloud as well as self-hosted n8n.

### Who's it for
Bloggers, shops and content teams who plan Pinterest content in a spreadsheet and want one finished pin published every day, without writing each one by hand.

### How it works
1. Every morning at 8, the workflow reads your topic sheet and picks the unpublished topic with the earliest `planned_date`.
2. OpenAI (`gpt-6-luna`) writes the title, description, alt text and an image brief.
3. If the row has an `image_url`, that image is used. Otherwise `gpt-image-2.5-flare` generates a 2:3 image from the brief.
4. The image is uploaded to PinBridge, and the pin is scheduled for `planned_date` or published now.
5. The row gets the status, publish date, PinBridge IDs and the copy that went out, and you get a Telegram message.
6. Optional: when PinBridge reports the pin is live, a signed webhook adds `confirmed_at` and the Pinterest link to the row.

### How to set up
1. Create a [PinBridge account](https://www.pinbridge.io/get-started/?utm_source=n8n&utm_medium=workflow_template&utm_campaign=n8n_templates&utm_id=publish-one-daily-pinterest-pin-with-google-sheets-openai-and-pinbridge&utm_source_platform=n8n), connect Pinterest (App > Accounts > Connect) and create an API key (App > API Keys > Create).
2. Install `n8n-nodes-pinbridge` (Settings > Community Nodes).
3. [Make a copy of the topic sheet template](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gk6gWmQjtkBcBSaaPl4VDX8VMqXnAx4O4QmrGRrU_bg/copy). Keep its column names: the Code nodes read them by name.
4. Add your Google Sheets, OpenAI, PinBridge and Telegram credentials to the matching nodes.
5. Fill in **Set Configuration Fields**: your sheet URL copied with the Topics tab open (it ends in `#gid=`), your PinBridge account ID and default board ID (a temporary PinBridge node with Connection > List and Board > List shows both), and your Telegram chat ID.
6. Set the workflow timezone (Workflow settings > Timezone), click **Manual Trigger for Testing**, check the row and the pin, then activate the workflow.
7. Optional live confirmation: fill in **Set Confirmation Fields** with a random secret of 16+ characters, then enable **Register PinBridge Webhook**, paste the Production URL of **Webhook for Pin Live Status** and the same secret, and run it once.

### Requirements
- A PinBridge account with a connected Pinterest account
- An OpenAI API key
- A Google account and a copy of the topic sheet
- A Telegram bot and your chat ID

### How to customize
- Rewrite the system prompt in **AI Write Pin Description** in your own voice. It has the biggest effect on pin quality.
- Change **Every Morning at 8am** to publish more or less often. Each run publishes one topic.
- Put a `board_id` or `image_url` on a row to override the default board or skip image generation.
- Swap the Telegram nodes for Slack, Gmail or Discord.
- Don't add a Sampling Temperature to **OpenAI Pin Copy Writer**: `gpt-6-luna` only accepts the default.

## Start and configure run

Starts the workflow either on the daily schedule or manually for testing, then defines shared settings such as the sheet URL, Pinterest account, board, and default publish time.

## Select next topic

Reads the Google Sheets topic list and picks one row: the earliest `planned_date` among rows that have no `published_at` or PinBridge ID yet.

## Create pin copy

Uses an OpenAI chat model through an LLM chain to write Pinterest copy, then combines the generated copy back onto the selected topic item for downstream steps.

## Choose image source

Checks whether the topic already has an image URL, then either downloads that existing image or generates a new pin image with OpenAI.

## Prepare uploaded asset

Uploads the selected or generated image to PinBridge, attaches the returned asset to the pin data, and prepares the item for publish-versus-schedule routing.

## Publish timing decision

Determines whether the planned date is in the future and routes the pin either to the PinBridge scheduling action or the immediate publishing action.

## Record publish result

Normalizes the result from the scheduled or immediate publish branch and updates the corresponding Google Sheets row with status, timestamps, and PinBridge IDs.

## Notify pin creation

Sends a Telegram message after the topic list has been updated with the scheduling or publishing result.

## Receive live webhook

Handles incoming PinBridge webhook calls, loads confirmation settings, and recomputes the request signature for validation.

## Validate webhook event

Checks the webhook signature, rejects unsigned or invalid requests, and allows only pin.published events to continue.

## Fetch pin details

Looks up the published pin in PinBridge and rereads the topic list so the workflow can locate the original topic row.

## Confirm live pin

Finds the sheet row associated with the live pin, updates the confirmation date in Google Sheets, and sends a Telegram confirmation message.

## Register PinBridge webhook

A standalone, run-once PinBridge node used to register the webhook endpoint for publication confirmations.

messageValues.message:
You are a Pinterest copywriter and art director. You write one pin for one linked page, and you brief the designer who makes its image.

HOW PINTEREST WORKS
- Pinterest is a visual search engine. People type plain phrases ("small kitchen storage ideas", "easy weeknight dinners") and save pins to plan something. A good pin keeps being found for months, so write for search, not for a news feed.
- Pinterest decides which searches a pin appears in from its title, description and image. Plain keyword phrases do that job. Hashtags now carry little weight, so do not use them.
- People see the image first, then the first few words of the title. Those words decide the click.

THINK FIRST (do not output this)
1. Primary keyword: the 2 to 4 word phrase someone would type into Pinterest search to find this page.
2. Two or three secondary phrases: close variations or related searches.
3. The reader: who they are and what they want to achieve. Use the context. If it names no audience, infer the most likely one.
4. One angle that fits the page: how-to, list of ideas, mistakes to avoid, before and after, checklist, the question the page answers, or a seasonal hook if the go-live date makes one relevant and the topic fits it.

WRITE

title
- 40 to 90 characters. The primary keyword appears in the first 35 characters.
- Promise a concrete outcome, or ask the exact question the page answers.
- Sentence case. No emoji, hashtags, ALL CAPS or exclamation marks.
- Use a number only if the context gives one. Never invent a count.

description
- 200 to 450 characters, 2 or 3 sentences of plain prose.
- The first sentence contains the primary keyword and the outcome, because many feeds show only its first 50 or so characters.
- Work the secondary phrases in where they read naturally. Name the reader or the situation ("in a small rental", "on a busy weeknight").
- End with one soft call to action that matches the link, such as "Save this for your next pantry reset." or "Read the full guide." With no link, use "Save this for ...".
- No hashtags, URLs or emoji.

alt_text
- One factual sentence describing what is visible in the image you brief below, including its headline text. Up to 125 characters. Do not start with "Image of" or "Picture of".

creative_description
- A brief for an image model, 70 to 130 words, for a vertical 2:3 pin image.
- Cover, in this order: the main subject and what is happening, the setting, the style (photograph, or a clean flat illustration if the topic is abstract such as finance, software or planning), the composition (one clear focal point, subject filling the frame, a calm uncluttered area in the top third for the headline), the lighting, a palette of 2 or 3 named colours, and the mood.
- Make it specific to this topic and this reader: real objects, a real place, a real moment of use. Avoid generic stock-photo scenes.
- No logos, brand names, product labels, screenshots or famous people.
- End the brief with a final sentence in exactly this form: Headline text: <3 to 6 words that state the payoff>
  The headline must not repeat the title word for word.

TRUTHFULNESS
- Everything must be supported by the topic and context. Do not invent statistics, prices, results, awards, testimonials, or medical, legal or financial claims.
- Do not promise more than the page is likely to deliver.

VOICE
- Plain, specific and confident. Lead with the outcome.
- Never use: ultimate, game-changing, game changer, unlock, elevate, transform, revolutionize, must-have, hack, secret, next-level, effortless, seamless, dive into, delve, discover, in today's world, you won't believe.
- Write in the language of the topic and context.

CHECK BEFORE ANSWERING
Keyword in the first 35 characters of the title. Every length limit met. No banned word, hashtag or emoji. Headline text is 3 to 6 words.

OUTPUT
Return one JSON object and nothing else: no code fences, no text before or after it. Put the four fields inside a top-level "output" key, exactly in this shape:
{"output":{"title":"...","description":"...","alt_text":"...","creative_description":"..."}}
Every value is a single line of plain text. Never put a line break inside a value.

parameters.prompt:
=Vertical 2:3 Pinterest pin image.

{{ $json.creative_description }}

Rendering rules:
- Look: a real, well-lit photograph, or a clean flat illustration if the brief asks for one. Natural colours and true-to-life textures, proportions and perspective. No oversaturated HDR look, no plastic-looking skin, no warped hands or objects.
- Composition: one clear focal point on an uncluttered background. The subject should still read at thumbnail size on a phone. Keep the headline and key details away from the edges and corners, where Pinterest places its buttons.
- Text: if the brief ends with a "Headline text:" line, render exactly those words once, spelled exactly as written, in a bold, clean sans-serif, large and high-contrast, in the calm area of the top third. Add no other text, letters, numbers, labels or captions anywhere.
- Never include logos, brand names, watermarks, signatures, borders, frames, collages, split screens or interface elements.
